children: Utilities companies delivered largely positive earnings results this week, with most S&P 500 utilities reporting higher earnings year over year. Revenue performance was less uniform, as several companies missed analyst expectations and three recorded annual declines.
Utilities Earnings Roundup
Bottom Line:
Of the 14 companies reporting, 12 firms (86%) topped EPS estimates, 1 met expectations, and 1 missed consensus. On a Y/Y basis, 13 companies (93%) recorded earnings growth.
Top Line:
Of the 14 companies reporting, 9 firms (64%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 5 came in below analyst estimates. Meanwhile, 11 companies (79%) reported Y/Y revenue growth.
Here is a look at some utilities companies that reported earnings this week:
Southern Company
reported Q3 revenue of $8.84B, up 13.1% Y/Y, exceeding the $8.41B consensus. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.94, beating the $1.58 estimate and increasing from $1.60 in the year-ago quarter.
Duke Energy
posted Q3 revenue of $9.10B, up 6.6% Y/Y, topping the $8.97B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $1.99 outperformed the $1.76 estimate, compared with $1.81 a year earlier.
Entergy
reported Q3 revenue of $4.37B, up 14.6% Y/Y, exceeding the $4.15B consensus. Adjusted EPS rose 29.4% Y/Y to $1.98, beating the $1.55 estimate.
Evergy
posted Q3 revenue of $2.10B, up 15.8% Y/Y, compared with the $1.97B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $2.58 outperformed the $2.05 estimate and increased from $2.03 in the year-ago period.
Sempra
reported Q3 revenue of $3.19B, up 1.3% Y/Y, but below the $3.31B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $1.40 exceeded the $1.18 estimate, rising from $1.11 a year earlier.
Public Service Enterprise Group

reported Q3 revenue of $3.02B, down 6.5% Y/Y, and missing the $3.25B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $1.15 fell short of the $1.20 estimate, although it was slightly higher than $1.13 in the year-ago quarter.
Eversource Energy

posted Q3 revenue of $2.98B, down 7.5% Y/Y and below the $3.15B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $0.92 matched analyst expectations but declined 22.7% from $1.19 a year earlier, making it the only company among the 14 to report lower Y/Y earnings.
PPL
reported Q3 revenue of $2.50B, up 11.5% Y/Y, beating the $2.42B consensus. Ongoing EPS of $0.54 outperformed the $0.53 estimate, increasing from $0.48 a year earlier.
Earnings next week
In the coming week, investors will turn their attention to upcoming results from Constellation Energy
and NRG Energy
